_note: VENDORED VERDICT DATA. Every urgency line here is a fixed string. The model is never asked what a light means or what a puddle is, and cannot change any verdict on this page — same discipline as data/chemistry-safety.json, and for the same reason: 'that's fine to drive on' is a claim that can hurt someone. Nothing in this file clears a vehicle as safe to drive; the strongest wording available is 'get it checked'.

stop-now.label: STOP NOW
stop-now.line: Pull over as soon as it is safe to do so and switch the engine off.

dont-drive.label: DON'T DRIVE IT
dont-drive.line: Don't drive it — get it recovered or looked at where it stands.

today.label: TODAY
today.line: Get this looked at today rather than leaving it.

this-week.label: THIS WEEK
this-week.line: Book it in this week; don't ignore it.

when-convenient.label: WHEN CONVENIENT
when-convenient.line: Worth sorting when you get a chance.

always: I can't tell you a car is safe to drive — nobody can from a description or a photo.
If in doubt, the cheap option is a phone call to a garage; the expensive one is finding out.
unknownLeak: That doesn't match anything in my table, and I'm not going to guess at a fluid. Put clean cardboard under it overnight so you get a clear colour and position, and if it's more than a few drops or you can't identify it, have someone look before you drive.
unknownLight: That doesn't match a symbol in my table. The owner's manual has the full legend for your exact car and it is the authority here — mine is a common-symbols list, not your manufacturer's.

leaks.position: front centre, under the radiator or a hose
leaks.texture: watery, slightly slimy between the fingers, sweet smell
leaks.why: Losing coolant means the engine can overheat, and an overheated engine warps a head gasket in minutes — a cheap hose turns into an engine rebuild.
leaks.notice: Temperature gauge climbing above its normal position, or a sweet smell after a drive.
leaks.extra: Never open the cap to check it while it's hot.

leaks.position: middle of the car, under the engine
leaks.texture: slippery, thick, greasy, smells of oil
leaks.why: A small drip is common and often just a seal; a puddle is not. Oil pressure loss destroys an engine faster than any other fault on this list.
leaks.notice: Check the dipstick before driving. A low level plus a red oil light is the stop-now case.
leaks.extra: Note how big the patch is after a night parked — that's the number a garage will ask for.

leaks.position: middle-to-front, roughly under where your feet are
leaks.texture: oily but thinner than engine oil, distinctive slightly sharp smell
leaks.why: An automatic gearbox run low destroys itself quickly and is one of the most expensive repairs on a car.
leaks.notice: Slipping, delayed or harsh gear changes.
leaks.extra: Red fluid is worth taking seriously even in small amounts.

leaks.position: behind a wheel, or under the pedal area at the back of the engine bay
leaks.texture: slick and oily, feels slippery, does not evaporate
leaks.why: The braking system is sealed and hydraulic. If fluid is escaping, pressure is escaping, and brakes fail without much warning once air gets in.
leaks.notice: A pedal that feels soft, spongy or travels further than usual.
leaks.extra: This is the one leak on the list where the answer is simply: don't drive it, have it recovered.

leaks.position: front of the engine bay, often dripping near a front wheel
leaks.why: You keep steering when it runs out, but it gets very heavy suddenly, and the pump is damaged by running dry.
leaks.notice: A whine or groan when turning, especially at parking speed, and heavier steering.
leaks.extra: Red fluid at the front can be power steering or transmission — the position is what separates them.

leaks.position: anywhere near the front, often after a top-up
leaks.texture: watery, thin, smells of alcohol or detergent
leaks.why: Not a mechanical problem. A cracked bottle or a split pipe.
leaks.notice: The washers stop working or empty unusually fast.

leaks.position: under the passenger side, roughly mid-car
leaks.texture: plain water, no smell, no feel on the fingers, evaporates
leaks.why: Almost always nothing at all. Air conditioning dehumidifies the cabin air and the water has to go somewhere.
leaks.notice: It happens on warm days after running the air conditioning, and dries up.
leaks.extra: This is the single most common 'my car is leaking' panic, and the answer is usually that it isn't.

leaks.position: anywhere along the car, often towards the back
leaks.why: A fuel leak is an ignition source away from a fire, and hot exhaust parts run far above the ignition temperature.
leaks.notice: You will smell it before you see it.
leaks.extra: Don't start the engine. Get it recovered.

lights.name: Oil pressure warning
lights.symbol: red oil can with a drip
lights.means: The engine has lost oil pressure. This is not a 'low oil' reminder — it means oil is not reaching the bearings.
lights.why: An engine running without oil pressure can be destroyed in under a minute. Every second of running makes it worse.
lights.extra: Switch off first, check the level second.

lights.name: Coolant temperature warning
lights.why: Continuing to drive warps the cylinder head and blows the head gasket — the difference between a hose and a four-figure bill is usually about two miles.
lights.extra: Let it cool for at least half an hour before opening anything. Don't touch the cap while it's hot.

lights.name: Brake system warning
lights.symbol: exclamation mark in a circle, in brackets
lights.means: Either the handbrake is still on, or the brake system has a fault — low fluid or a pressure problem.
lights.why: If it isn't the handbrake, the system that stops the car is telling you it can't be relied on.
lights.extra: Release the handbrake fully. If it stays lit, that's the fault case, and the answer is recovery rather than a careful drive.

lights.name: Battery / charging warning
lights.means: The battery is not being charged — usually the alternator or its belt, not the battery itself.
lights.why: The car is running off stored charge and will stop when it runs out, wherever it happens to be at the time.
lights.extra: Turn off what you don't need — heated screen, air conditioning, stereo — and head somewhere useful rather than home.

lights.name: Check engine / malfunction indicator
lights.means: The engine management system has logged a fault. Steady amber is 'get it read'; FLASHING is a misfire and is much more serious.
lights.why: A steady light is often something small like a sensor or a loose fuel cap, but it also switches off the emissions monitoring that would catch something bigger.
lights.extra: A flashing check-engine light is a stop-now case, not a this-week case: raw fuel is going into the catalytic converter. This is the light that needs a code reader — I can't read the code, and guessing at one sends you replacing the wrong part.

lights.name: ABS warning
lights.means: The anti-lock system has a fault. Normal braking still works; the anti-lock function may not.
lights.why: You'll only discover it's missing during an emergency stop on a poor surface, which is the worst possible time to find out.
lights.extra: Leave more room than usual until it's fixed.

lights.name: Airbag / SRS warning
lights.symbol: seated figure with a circle in front
lights.means: The restraint system has a fault and the airbags may not deploy in a crash.
lights.why: Nothing about how the car drives changes, which is exactly why people leave it — and it only matters once.
lights.extra: This is a job for a garage. Airbag components are explosive and are not a DIY item.

lights.name: Tyre pressure warning
lights.symbol: horseshoe / cross-section of a tyre with an exclamation mark
lights.means: At least one tyre is significantly below its correct pressure — or it's simply gone cold overnight.
lights.why: An underinflated tyre overheats, wears out fast and handles badly, and a slow puncture only gets worse.
lights.extra: Check all four cold with a gauge against the sticker in the driver's door shut. If one keeps dropping, it's a puncture.

lights.name: Power steering warning
lights.symbol: steering wheel with an exclamation mark
lights.means: Power assistance has a fault or has been reduced.
lights.why: The steering still works but can go heavy without warning, which is a genuine surprise at parking speed.

lights.name: Glow plug / pre-heat (diesel)
lights.means: Normal on a cold start — it goes out when the engine is ready to crank. Staying on or flashing afterwards is a fault.
lights.why: Flashing usually points at the engine management on a diesel rather than the glow plugs themselves.
